seoTitle: How to Add Multiple Quantity to an eBay Listing
metaDescription: Learn how to add bulk quantity to a single eBay listing in 2026 so buyers can purchase multiple units without creating separate listings.
intro: If you sell identical items in bulk — phone cases, stationery, handmade crafts, anything you stock more than one of — putting them all under a single listing with a quantity field beats duplicating the listing for every unit. Buyers pick how many they want from one page, your Seller Hub tracks the remaining stock for you, and your store stays cleaner because you're not competing with your own duplicate listings in search. This guide walks through where the quantity setting actually lives when you create a fixed-price listing, and what to watch once it's live so you don't oversell.

steps.heading: Start a fixed-price listing
steps.body: Multiple quantity only works on fixed-price listings, not auction-style ones — an auction sells a single item to a single winning bidder, so there's nothing to split across buyers. Head to Seller Hub and either create a new listing or resume one sitting in your drafts, then make sure you're building it as a straightforward Buy It Now listing rather than an auction before you get to the pricing details.

steps.heading: Set the format to Buy It Now and enter your quantity
steps.body: In the Pricing section, the Format dropdown lets you switch between Auction and Buy It Now — select Buy It Now if it isn't already chosen. Directly below it sits the Quantity field, which defaults to 1. Change that number to however many identical units you actually have in stock; this is the number eBay will offer buyers up to, and the number it counts down as sales come in. Leave "Require immediate payment when buyer uses Buy It Now" checked if you want funds secured the moment someone buys, which is worth doing on higher-volume bulk listings.

image.caption: The Pricing section of a listing, with Format set to Buy It Now and the Quantity field just below it — this is where you tell eBay how many units are available.

steps.heading: Check how it appears in Seller Hub
steps.body: Once saved, the listing shows up in Seller Hub under Listings, whether it's still a draft, scheduled, or active. The table there displays your available quantity in the Av. Qty column alongside the price, format, and duration, so you can scan your whole inventory at once instead of opening each listing individually. Duration is worth noting too — a bulk listing set to "Good 'Til Cancelled" stays live and keeps selling units until you end it or your quantity runs out, rather than expiring after a fixed number of days.

image.caption: The Manage drafts view in Seller Hub, showing the Av. Qty, Buy It Now format, and Good 'Til Cancelled duration columns for a saved listing.

steps.heading: Let buyers pick their own quantity
steps.body: Once the listing goes live, buyers see a quantity selector right on the item page instead of a plain "Buy It Now" button with no options. They choose how many units they want in that single checkout, which means someone who wants three phone cases doesn't have to place three separate orders — and you don't have to process three separate shipments' worth of admin for what could've been one package.

steps.heading: Let eBay track the stock for you
steps.body: Every completed sale automatically reduces the quantity you set, so there's no manual step where you have to log back in and lower a number after each order. This is the main reason bulk listings save time over duplicate single-item listings — with duplicates, you're either manually ending listings as they sell or risking two buyers both winning the same physical item.

steps.heading: Keep the number accurate to avoid overselling
steps.body: Automatic tracking only works if the quantity you entered actually matches what you have on hand. If stock moves outside of eBay — a sale at a craft fair, damaged inventory, a restock — update the listing's quantity promptly so eBay isn't still offering units you can't fulfill. Overselling on a bulk listing is one of the fastest ways to rack up cancellations and dented seller metrics, so treat this number as something you check, not something you set once and forget.

faq.question: Can I add multiple quantity to an auction-style eBay listing?
faq.answer: No, multiple quantity is only available on fixed-price 'Buy It Now' listings, not traditional auction-style listings, since an auction resolves to one winning bidder.

faq.question: Does eBay automatically update my stock count as items sell?
faq.answer: Yes. The Quantity field decreases automatically with each completed sale, which is what you see reflected in the Av. Qty column in Seller Hub.

faq.question: Can I use multiple quantity with Good 'Til Cancelled listings?
faq.answer: Yes — Good 'Til Cancelled listings with a quantity set will keep selling units continuously until you end the listing or the stock runs out, rather than expiring after a set number of days.

faq.question: Where do I check how much stock is left on a bulk listing?
faq.answer: Open Seller Hub → Listings, where the Av. Qty column shows remaining stock for every active, scheduled, or draft listing without needing to open each one.

faq.question: Is adding bulk quantity better than creating separate listings?
faq.answer: Usually yes — it keeps your store cleaner, consolidates buyer interest and reviews onto one listing, and lets eBay handle inventory countdown automatically instead of you managing several near-identical listings by hand.
